name: Kept
tagline: You can smell a fake from across the room. The real thing, too.
epigraph: The makers of one bottle in this glass chose not to make more.
language_row: Wren's resonance: not yet on v1 (four sibling frames caught), ready on v2. Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour, except the plain garnish words "a strip of lemon peel" (twelve pours; a garnish, not a motif). No gendered words.
sources: Fact card `_studio/fact-cards/chartreuse-2023-cap.md` (Oxford CHARTREUSE pdf 439–440, ARMAGNAC pdf 137; the house's January 2023 letter to its partners, quoted at length in *The Daily Pour*, 2 March 2023; VinePair c. 2023, relaying Jason Wilson's Substack, for the shortages; *InsideHook* 2022 importer gloss, kept out). Drink: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 29, 157, 176, 188; Arnold's built band. Set aside: `thad-vogler-bar-agricole.md`, `floc-de-gascogne.md`. Room notes `work/outlaw-innocent/`.
names_note: Kept (Wren; Tomás with tagline 3; Hester's pick was What It's For, which named the y5 position the room gave up as On Their Behalf's). Also considered: Less, on Purpose; Spoken For.
open_items: The plan's lead, Thad Vogler, failed Wren's point 4: after the book his bars all closed (by May 2025), he sells spirits under his own label and lends his name to a canned vodka soda; Hoodline (relaying Eater) reports wage-theft claims, unread at source. Wren: for this person a story cut off before that is the lie they'd catch. The Germain-Robin backup failed too (Gallo, 2017).

The Chartreuse story rests on the house's letter as quoted by The Daily Pour and on VinePair; the 2021/2023 decision is on no library page. The letter is written about the monks, in the third person, so it is never "their letter".

Point 1 (refused because it was false) passes on Wren's reframe, false to who you are, and point 3 (the price) passes narrowly, on the disappointment of the people who loved it. Hester left both to Wren.

Makeable: yellow Chartreuse is under the same allocation (the letter's plural, "the Chartreuse liqueurs") and can be hard to find; a 700 ml bottle holds about 46 tablespoons. Another Alpine herbal liqueur loses the story. Armagnac 40–43% straight; stronger at 2,400 ÷ ABV ml with water to 60 ml.
Kept out: the planet reason (Left Standing's ground), the elixir and the formula (medicine; Beside the First), the 1903 expulsion, "still" about the monks, "dry" (7.11 g sugar: lightly sweet).
